why: The item is a definition. IsTopGoodPoint and IsTopBadPoint are vocabulary; A (universe 0) is the type of the one listed theorem, dimPart_topDim_eq_of_isTopGoodPoint (p. 456: Θ_k agrees at a point of U ∩ U' that is top-good for two labelled structures). B says the project's IsTopGoodPoint / IsTopBadPoint are the blind notions at every y ∈ M^k_U. B holds outright (B_holds). On M^k_U the definitions differ only in two places: the project asks y ∈ M_U, which y ∈ M^k_U implies, and V ⊆ U, which we get by replacing V with V ∩ U. M^k_U, topDim and the top-bad clause agree by rfl. B's branched hypothesis and labels are not needed. B ⇒ A: A is not a consequence of a statement about definitions. It is re-proved outright (A_outright, the project's proof copied, from non-item lemmas). Both directions are therefore vacuous. The content is that on M^k_U, the only place the text defines them, the definitions agree. Off M^k_U the project's IsTopGoodPoint holds at every point of M_U, vacuously; B makes no claim there.
